_comment: Scoring weights, thresholds, labels, and category mapping for vendor_audit. The branching logic in audit_checks.py reads from this file. Each entry under 'weights' is {earned, possible} keyed by score outcome label. 'possible' is the denominator that always applies for that outcome; 'earned' is the value awarded in the named outcome. An outcome with possible=0 is never counted in either numerator or denominator (used for partial checks where absence proves nothing).
_comment_categories: Each scored item maps to one of six top-level categories used in both the detailed sections and the summary. Categories: Email, DNS, Routing, TLS, HTTP, Website. Items not listed here fall back to 'Website' which is the catch-all for origin-side concerns.

weights._comment_email: Email - SPF/DMARC are the highest-impact controls a domain can publish; weighted accordingly.
weights._comment_dmarc_rua: Without rua=, operators can't see who's spoofing them or whether legit mail is being rejected, so a deployment is operating blind.
weights._comment_mx_target_hygiene: RFC 2181 §10.3 and RFC 5321 §5.1: MX RDATA must be a domain name (not an IP literal) AND that name must resolve directly to A/AAAA records (not via a CNAME). Real sending MTAs vary in how they handle violations — Postfix warns; some receivers bounce. Worst-of: ANY MX with a CNAME target OR ANY MX as IP literal scores 0/1. clean = 1/1. no_mx = 0/0 (the MX-records check above already covered absence).
weights._comment_email_transport: Mail transport hardening - only scored when MX exists.
weights._comment_starttls_mx: STARTTLS-MX probe (--deep). For each MX host we open TCP/25, EHLO, STARTTLS, and inspect the negotiated TLS version. Worst-of aggregation across hosts: an attacker can MITM the lowest-preference MX, so the weakest host defines the actual exposure. tls_1_3 → 2/2 (full credit, modern TLS); tls_1_2 → 1.5/2 (acceptable but TLS 1.3 is now widely supported and a half-point penalty rewards operators who upgrade); tls_legacy → 1/2 (TLS 1.0/1.1 negotiated; encrypted but vulnerable); no_starttls → 0/2 (server didn't advertise STARTTLS at EHLO, mail is plaintext on the wire); unprobed → 0/0 (port 25 blocked egress, connection timeout, or other network error — we couldn't conclude anything). The unprobed row is intentionally still emitted into the breakdown (rather than silently dropped) so the operator sees the check was attempted and the reason it produced no signal — silent disappearance would let an operator wrongly conclude STARTTLS is fine when it was just unprobed.
weights._comment_dkim: DKIM common-selector probe is a partial check - selectors are operator-chosen and arbitrary, so absence at our six common names proves nothing. Score 'found' as 1/1 (positive evidence). Score 'not_found' as 0/0 (no evidence either way - drops out of the denominator entirely so we don't penalise domains using uncommon selector names).
weights._comment_dkim_strength: DKIM key strength scores the WORST observed key across all found selectors. Only scored when at least one selector was found (not_found drops out, same logic as DKIM common-selector probe). Ed25519 and RSA-2048+ score full credit; RSA-1024 (deprecated by RFC 8301) scores partial; RSA <1024 (broken) scores zero. 'unparseable' (we found a record but couldn't read the key) scores 0/0 — no signal either way. 'revoked' (operator explicitly disabled the selector via empty p=) scores 0/0 — deliberate operator action, not a finding.
weights._comment_routing: Routing - IPv6 reachability + RPKI/IRR per address family.
weights._comment_dnssec: DNSSEC weighting rationale: the TLD being signed is not the operator's choice (most are signed by default), so it's worth 1 not 3. The AD flag is the only check that proves the validation chain actually works end-to-end - that's worth 3.
weights._comment_authoritative_delegation: RFC 1034 §4.2: an NS listed at the parent registry MUST set the AA (Authoritative Answer) flag when queried for its own zone. An NS that doesn't is 'lame' — listed in delegation but not actually serving the zone. Worst-of: ANY lame NS scores 0/1, since users routed to that NS (luck of the resolver) get NODATA or SERVFAIL. unprobed = 0/0 (we couldn't reach any NS to test, no signal).
weights._comment_open_resolver: RFC 5358 / BCP 140: an authoritative NS should not also serve recursion to arbitrary clients. An open resolver is usable as a DNS amplification reflector in DDoS attacks. Worst-of: ANY NS that returned a recursive answer for our third-party probe (cloudflare.com) scores 0/1. unprobed = 0/0.
weights._comment_tls: TLS / certificate / HSTS - together describe the transport-security posture.
weights._comment_chain_completeness: Server-side chain completeness — server SHOULD send leaf + every needed intermediate so clients don't fall back to AIA fetching. Compares OpenSSL's verified chain length against what the server actually sent. 'unsupported' covers Python <3.13 (the API was added in 3.13); scored 0/0 to keep results stable across Python versions.
weights._comment_hsts_preloaded: Four outcomes. 'preloaded' = on the live HSTS preload list, full credit. 'pending' = submitted to hstspreload.org AND accepted, waiting for the next Chromium release rollup (typically 2-3 months from submission). 'preload_directive' = header has the preload directive but the domain isn't on the list and hasn't been accepted to pending — operator may have set the directive without submitting. 'pending' and 'preload_directive' both score 0.5/1: deliberate operator action toward preloading, but not yet shipped to users. The renderer distinguishes the two so vendors who already submitted aren't told to submit again.
weights._comment_ssl_labs: SSL Labs is weighted at 5 points. A higher weight would make it the single largest contributor and overlap substantially with the locally-checked TLS items above. Five points is enough to materially reward A+/A grades and penalise F/T/M, while leaving the locally-checked TLS posture (TLS 1.3, cert lifetime, name match, HSTS) as the dominant signal in this category.
weights._comment_http: HTTP - version + redirect hygiene. 'HTTP version' uses three tiers: http3=2/2 (modern, full credit), http2=1/2 (legacy but still encrypted, half credit), http1=0/2 (no HTTP/2 support — server should be retired).
weights._comment_www_apex_unified: Mozilla deployment guidance: pick one canonical web hostname (apex OR www) and redirect the other variant to it, so a user typing either form lands at the same page. We don't score the CHOICE of canonical form — apex-canonical and www-canonical both pass — only the unification. 'split' (both serve content but neither redirects) and 'half_missing' (one variant has no A/AAAA, so users typing it get DNS errors) both score 0/1. 'unified' is full credit. 'not_scored' (both unreachable / DNS errors) is 0/0 — no signal.
weights._comment_website: Website - origin-side hygiene: server header disclosure, security headers, cookies, security.txt, clock, page-level deep checks.
weights._comment_error_page: Default error-page disclosure — operators who care about disclosure customise/strip default 404 pages. Detection uses fingerprints in error_page_fingerprints.json (layout-specific patterns to keep FPs low). 'spa_or_2xx' (no 404 to inspect) and 'error' (probe failed) score 0/0 — no signal.
weights._comment_cors: CORS configuration — only scored when broken. Absence of CORS is the SECURE DEFAULT (browsers refuse cross-origin reads without ACAO) and not a finding. Three failure modes are detected: ACAO=* combined with credentials=true (spec-forbidden pairing), ACAO=null (trusts sandboxed origins), and reflective ACAO (server echoes whatever Origin: the client sent — any origin trusted). 'no_cors' (passing default) scores 0/0; weak configurations score 0/1.
weights._comment_reporting_endpoints: Reporting endpoints — combined check across Report-To (legacy), Reporting-Endpoints (modern), and NEL. Operator opt-in for collecting CSP/network/feature-policy violation reports. Presence of any of the three is a maturity signal (1/1). Absence is NOT a finding (most sites don't bother) — scored 0/0 so it doesn't dilute the denominator for sites that haven't opted in.
weights._comment_csp_detail: Detailed CSP analysis derived from Google CSP Evaluator.
weights._comment_deep: --deep-only checks. Only counted toward score when --deep was used.

score_label_display.DKIM (common selectors): DKIM key found at common selector(s)
score_label_display.DKIM key strength: DKIM key strength acceptable (Ed25519 or RSA ≥2048)
score_label_display.Cert chain completeness: Server sends complete certificate chain (no AIA fallback needed)
score_label_display.Default error page: Default error page customised (no server disclosure)
score_label_display.Reporting endpoints: Operator collects violation reports (Report-To / Reporting-Endpoints / NEL)
score_label_display.NS not open resolver: Authoritative nameservers do not also serve open recursion (RFC 5358 / BCP 140)
score_label_display.MX target hygiene: MX targets are hostnames (not IP literals) and resolve directly to A/AAAA (no CNAME) (RFC 2181 §10.3)
score_label_display.CSP script-src safety: CSP script-src is strict (nonce/hash, strict-dynamic, or 'none')
score_label_display.Redirect first-hop hygiene: First redirect hop goes to HTTPS on same host
score_label_display.www and apex unified: Apex and www variants unified (one redirects to the other)
score_label_display.Server clock accuracy: Server clock in sync with UTC
score_label_display.Mixed content (in-page): No mixed content in page body

HTTP version.http1: HTTP/1.1 only — server does not support HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 (http1mustdie.com)

partial_label.IPv4 RPKI: IPv4 RPKI not-found - no ROA published, prefix unprotected
partial_label.IPv6 RPKI: IPv6 RPKI not-found - no ROA published, prefix unprotected
partial_label.HTTP\u2192HTTPS redirect: Port 80 open but not redirecting to HTTPS

HSTS preloaded._comment: Multi-tier outcome — 'pending' (submitted to hstspreload.org, accepted, waiting for next Chrome rollup) and 'preload_directive' (header has preload, never submitted) both score 0.5/1 but get different finding text. Reader: see _resolve_partial_label() in audit_txt_report.py / audit_render.py
HSTS preloaded._default: HSTS preload directive present but not on preload list yet
HSTS preloaded.pending: HSTS preload submission pending — accepted by hstspreload.org, waiting for the next Chrome release rollup (typically 2–3 months)
HSTS preloaded.preload_directive: HSTS preload directive present but the domain has not been submitted to hstspreload.org

partial_label.Server header: Server header discloses software name (no version)
partial_label.Referrer-Policy: Referrer-Policy present but using a weak value
partial_label.CSP: CSP present but permissive (wildcard src detected)
partial_label.security.txt: security.txt present but Expires: field missing or expired
partial_label.DMARC policy: DMARC policy: quarantine - not yet at reject
partial_label.SPF policy: SPF soft fail only (~all) - not fully enforcing
partial_label.TLS connection: TLS running but certificate is untrusted (self-signed/expired)
partial_label.Certificate name match: TLS running but certificate is untrusted (self-signed/expired)
partial_label.Certificate lifetime: Certificate lifetime exceeds 199 days - manual renewal likely
partial_label.DANE TLSA on MX: DANE/TLSA on some but not all MX hosts

CSP script-src safety._comment: Multi-tier outcome — different partial outcomes need different text. Reader: see _resolve_partial_label() in audit_txt_report.py / audit_render.py
CSP script-src safety.nonce_or_hash: CSP script-src uses nonce/hash (good; strict-dynamic would be stronger)
CSP script-src safety.host_allowlist: CSP script-src uses host allowlist (weaker than nonce/hash)

partial_label.Mixed content (in-page): Passive mixed content present (images/media over HTTP)
partial_label.Server clock accuracy: Server clock skew is small but noticeable
partial_label.Subresource Integrity: Some external scripts have SRI but not all
partial_label.CAA records: CAA present but no iodef= reporting contact

DKIM key strength._comment: Multi-tier outcome — different outcomes need different finding text. Reader: see _resolve_partial_label() in audit_txt_report.py / audit_render.py
DKIM key strength.weak: DKIM key uses RSA-1024 (deprecated by RFC 8301 — upgrade to RSA-2048+ or Ed25519)
DKIM key strength.unparseable: DKIM key found but could not be parsed
DKIM key strength.revoked: DKIM key explicitly revoked (p= empty) — deliberate operator action

Default error page._comment: Multi-tier outcome — different outcomes need different finding text. Reader: see _resolve_partial_label() in audit_txt_report.py / audit_render.py
Default error page.default_no_version: Default error page detected (server software disclosed, no version)
Default error page.default_with_version: Default error page detected with version disclosure
Default error page.spa_or_2xx: Default error page check did not run (probe returned 2xx/3xx — SPA shell, wildcard route, or WAF redirect)
Default error page.error: Default error page check could not run (probe failed)

www and apex unified._comment: Multi-tier outcome — 'half_missing' carries a missing_side ('apex' or 'www') that the renderer substitutes into a 'half_missing_apex' / 'half_missing_www' key. Reader: see _resolve_partial_label() in audit_txt_report.py / audit_render.py
www and apex unified._default: Apex and www variants are not unified
www and apex unified.split: Apex and www both serve content but neither redirects to the other (split-brain site)
www and apex unified.half_missing: Only one of apex / www has DNS records — users typing the other form get a DNS error
www and apex unified.half_missing_apex: Apex has no A/AAAA records — users typing the bare domain get a DNS error
www and apex unified.half_missing_www: www variant has no A/AAAA records — users typing www get a DNS error

partial_label.Authoritative delegation: At least one nameserver listed at the parent registry is lame — it does not answer authoritatively for this zone
partial_label.NS not open resolver: At least one authoritative nameserver also serves open recursion — abusable for DNS amplification attacks (RFC 5358)

MX target hygiene._comment: Multi-tier outcome — separate keys for CNAME-only, IP-only, and both, so the finding can name what's wrong. Reader: see _resolve_partial_label() in audit_txt_report.py / audit_render.py
MX target hygiene.cname_target: At least one MX target is a CNAME, not a direct A/AAAA (RFC 2181 §10.3 violation)
MX target hygiene.ip_literal: At least one MX target is an IP literal, not a hostname (RFC 2181 §10.3 / RFC 5321 §5.1 violation)
MX target hygiene.cname_and_ip: MX targets include both an IP literal and a CNAME target (RFC 2181 §10.3 / RFC 5321 §5.1 violations)

_comment_scoring_policy_eol: Per-library 0/1 scoring for detected EOL libraries, per-OS 0/3 scoring for detected EOL operating systems. Both implementations work the same way: score_results() in audit_checks.py iterates the relevant list (results['versioned_libs']['libraries'] for libs, results['os_eol']['os_findings'] for OSes) after all other checks and appends per-finding tuples with hardcoded weights (libraries are 0/1, OSes are 0/3). The rubric does NOT contain weight entries for these labels — they're appended directly. Category resolution falls through to 'Website' (the catch-all), which is the correct destination.
_comment_starttls_mx_aggregation: STARTTLS-MX is scored worst-CONFIRMED-of across MX hosts. Severity ordering of confirmed outcomes (worst → best): no_starttls > tls_legacy > tls_1_2 > tls_1_3. Unprobed hosts are dropped from the aggregation when ANY confirmed result exists — a network error on one host (port 25 blocked egress, timeout, refused connection) does not pull down the score for a domain where other MX hosts produced clean handshakes. Only when EVERY host was unprobed does the entire check evaluate to 'unprobed' (0/0). The 0/0 row still appears in the breakdown rather than being silently dropped, so the operator sees the check ran but produced no signal.
